cards.english: Show your ticket.
This way is shorter.
That road is longer.
This street is narrower.
Life is getting better.
That park is greener.
His voice is lower.
Her voice is higher.
This is my book.
cards.existing: For 'whose?', ask `чей/чья/чьё/чьи?` – same gender/number agreement: `чей это дом?` (whose house is this?).

cards.english: These are my friends.
This is your seat.
Her dress is new.
Our teacher is strict.
Our apartment is big.
Their car broke down.
Our school is new.
Your order is ready.
Summer is warmer than spring.
The days are getting longer.
He is the most prepared.
Their children study well.
I took my book.
They invited their friends.
Their vacation starts tomorrow.
He lost his passport.
My friend likes music.
She helps her mom.
He runs faster than me.
He is the smartest student.
She is happier than before.
We write to our friends.
It's fun with my friend.
Yesterday I read an interesting article.
The store has been open since morning.
She became more confident.
cards.existing: Common idioms: `у себя` (at one's place), `с собой` (with oneself / for takeaway), `по себе` (according to one's self).

cards.english: Her children study at school.
My sister lives in Moscow.
We sold our old car.
My brother has a dog.
My sister has a cat.
What happened cannot be changed.
She is used to her room.
Instead of tea I want coffee.
A clean lake is behind the forest.
Near our house there is a park.

cards.target: То ли дождь, то ли снег.
cards.english: Either rain or snow.

cards.target: Кто рано встаёт, тому бог подаёт.
cards.english: The early bird gets the worm.

cards.target: Поезд, на котором мы ехали, опоздал.
cards.english: The train we were on was late.

cards.target: Она нашла место, где можно отдохнуть.
cards.english: She found a place where one can rest.

cards.target: Я помню свой первый день в школе.
cards.english: I remember my first day at school.

cards.target: Это мой дом, я живу здесь уже десять лет.
cards.english: This is my house, I've lived here for ten years already.
Whose child is crying?
She is more patient than mom.
The river is deeper than the lake.
The mountain is higher than the hill.
This is a more comfortable armchair.
This cake is the most delicious.
The milk is warmer than usual.
He is richer than his neighbor.
The TV is louder than necessary.
This is the most important question.
This is the least difficult task.
My female friend likes to dance.
Without my permission it's not allowed.
Opposite their school is a store.
Moscow is the most beautiful of all cities.
The air is fresher outside the city.
The bridge is stronger than they thought.
The wall is thinner than it seemed.
This is the worst movie of the year.
The deepest lake is Baikal.
The longest river is the Volga.
He is more attentive than before.
The music is quieter than desired.
She takes care of her children.
One's own home is the best.
The most beautiful girl in the class.
The teacher whom everyone respects is leaving.
cards.existing: `Книга, которую я читаю` (the book that I'm reading – `книгу` is feminine, accusative because it's the object of `читаю`).

cards.english: He is the best student in the group.
The quieter you go, the further you'll get.
The children to whom we read fell asleep.
cards.existing: Compare: `Мужчина, который пришёл` (the man who came – nominative, subject) vs `мужчина, которого я знаю` (the man whom I know – accusative).

cards.target: Самый высокий дом на этой улице.
cards.english: The tallest building on this street.

cards.target: Она такая же умная, как мама.
cards.english: She is as smart as mom.

cards.target: Женщина, которой я помог, поблагодарила меня.
cards.english: The woman whom I helped thanked me.
cards.existing: Put a comma before `который` (Russian punctuation rule). The clause is set off by commas on both sides if it's in the middle.

cards.target: Причина, по которой он опоздал, понятна.
cards.english: The reason he was late is understandable.
cards.existing: Compare: `Мужчина, который пришёл` (the man who came – nominative, subject) vs `мужчина, которого я знаю` (the man whom I know – accusative).

cards.target: Автор, чья книга стала бестселлером, приехал.
cards.english: The author whose book became a bestseller arrived.

cards.target: Друзья, благодаря которым я выучил русский.
cards.english: Friends thanks to whom I learned Russian.

cards.target: Чем раньше встанешь, тем больше успеешь.
cards.english: The earlier you get up, the more you accomplish.

cards.target: Учёный, чьи работы известны, получил награду.
cards.english: The scientist whose works are known received an award.

cards.target: Мальчик, чья мама – врач, хочет стать врачом.
cards.english: The boy whose mom is a doctor wants to become a doctor.
